Updated assessment with Beige Book context:
- Policy stance: Still solidly dovish (0–0.25% fed funds rate, ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases, AIT-consistent guidance).
- Beige Book activity: Most districts reported modest-to-moderate growth with improving consumer spending; auto sales up but constrained by inventories; travel and tourism firming on vaccine rollout; housing activity strong.
- Constraints and risks: Acute labor supply shortages—especially for qualified workers—and supply chain disruptions continue to weigh on production and raise cost pressures. Employment gains are uneven across industries and skills.
- Credit conditions: Consistent with SLOOS, business lending remains cautious—particularly for smaller firms—while mortgage credit standards eased, aligning with strong housing demand and Fed MBS purchases.

Net tone: Stronger demand signals and vaccine-driven reopening support a slightly more positive outlook than before, tempered by persistent labor and supply bottlenecks. Policy remains appropriately accommodative and risk-aware.
